    "hypothesis": "Predicted that nonface objects containing salient Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, and continuity) would elicit holistic processing similar to that observed for faces, even in the absence of expertise.",
    "design": "mixed, with task (faces vs. line patterns) as a between-subjects factor and alignment (aligned vs. misaligned) and congruency (congruent vs. incongruent) as within-subjects factors.",
    "manipulation_or_predictor": "The presence of Gestalt information in line patterns (connectedness, closure, and continuity) compared to faces, and the alignment of top and bottom parts of the stimuli.",
    "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d') in a composite task, where participants judge whether the top parts of two stimuli are the same or different while ignoring the bottom parts.",
    "population_and_setting": "22 participants recruited at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics.",
    "sample_size_total": 22,
    "recruitment_and_incentive": "Not stated.",
    "analysis_plan": "A 2 (alignment) x 2 (congruency) x 2 (task) repeated measures ANOVA to test for a congruency effect and a congruency by alignment interaction.",
    "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
    "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks (faces and line patterns). The composite task used a complete design where the target top parts were either the same or different, and the irrelevant bottom parts were either congruent or incongruent with the top parts, presented in either aligned or misaligned configurations."
